answer: Picture an agent economy as a reef: dense, interdependent, and unforgiving of impostors. Each agent's identity sits on a knoll of costly work — GPU-hours of attestations staked in escrow, burned if it misbehaves. A new identity entering the network must anchor to that reef gradually, earning trust-weight vertex by vertex across a verified history graph; spinning up ten thousand fake identities buys no influence because each vertex of the trust graph is backed by stake and time, so sybils stay lightweight, unstaked, and powerless.
